findings.asked: Factorise using the difference of two squares with a fractional coefficient; then factorise an expression in three variables.
findings.wentWrong: Most scored zero on the fractional case. In the second, most took out 'a' and then stopped or could not handle the x and y terms; partial credit for leaving 'a' inside one bracket with the rest right.
findings.rule: After the common factor, look for a squared minus b squared even when a or b is a fraction or a product of letters.

findings.asked: Factorise an expression with three letters using a common factor and the difference of two squares.
findings.wentWrong: A mark for taking 2 out, then trouble with the three letters.
findings.rule: Treat 4x squared y squared as (2xy) squared.

findings.asked: Factorise fully with a common factor of 3a followed by the difference of two squares.
findings.wentWrong: Most took 3a out; only top candidates recognised the remaining difference of two squares.
findings.rule: Factorise 'fully' means keep going until nothing more factorises.

ruleToRemember: Highest common factor first (numbers and letters), then check the bracket for a squared minus b squared, where a and b can be fractions or products of letters.
aStarSignal: Spotting the difference of two squares after a common factor when the terms are fractions or involve three letters.
